title: Wednesday's page
how: Everything here passed my check and a blind reviewer's for obvious faults; the reviewer's remaining notes are beside each. Pick one per item; a note is optional. Your picks save on the page.

Updated Tuesday evening. Your picks of Tuesday morning are acted on and off the page: Sheila's face is S4, with its hair, and goes into the game tonight; Ron's threat keeps the game's own voice (your blind B); Ron's and Darren's voices, their thinking sounds, the conversation light and how Sheila looks at you are approved; Darren's face waits on a man's haircut.

Left for you: the street by day and at night, as whole frames; Darren with a man's haircut; and two calls, each with my recommendation. Under your narrowed rule the pillar box's and kiosk's marks are mine within canon (every brand is fictional): made-up marks.
foot: Anything you do not pick carries onto the next page.

sections.name: The street, with its 1990 clutter
sections.note: The street as the game draws it now, by day. New in it: a KX100 telephone kiosk, a pillar box, galvanised dustbins, cast-iron bollards, council litter bins, a telegraph pole with its wires to the houses, and a grit bin at the top of the street. Each passed my check and a blind reviewer's, which under your rule is their approval; the pillar box and kiosk carry no marks until you choose them. Say if anything jars. The blind reviewer's remaining notes: the kiosk's glass shows no tint or reflection, so it reads a little like an empty frame; the telegraph wires two to the flats opposite seem to end at the chimneys from the far end of the street, and no feed cable reaches the pole; the dustbins and the pillar box's foot are mostly hidden by cars and people in these views. (Its two other notes, the wires' sag and the litter bin crowding the lamp post, are fixed in these frames.)

sections.name: The street at night, under its sodium lamps
sections.note: "Later that week, evening" used to play in broad daylight; it now plays at night. The lamps are low-pressure sodium, one orange colour, lighting pools under each lamp with the gaps between left dark, and the wet road carries their reflections (from the research on 1990 street light). It passed my check and a blind reviewer's. Say if it reads as night to you, and if the orange is right. The blind reviewer's remaining notes: the left terrace's brick is lit almost evenly up to the eaves, closer to floodlighting than to pools; across the road the upper brick is brighter than the pavement in front of Rita's; the wet road carries few streaks from the lamps; colours survive the sodium light (the green stripes, the green bin), where under real sodium they would go orange and black; the cream tiles under the right-hand shop are the brightest patch; that shop's window reads as a board; the lit upstairs windows read cool grey-green rather than warm. Fixed since the first try, in these frames: lamps that pool light on the pavement, the town's orange glow in the sky, lit windows on the hillside and upstairs, and shops lit inside.

sections.name: Darren Milner, with a man's haircut
sections.note: His S4 face, which you turned down for its long hair, now with Epic's short casual cut and his bleached ends. It passed my check and a fresh reviewer's. The reviewer's remaining notes: it is not a grown-out perm (no wave, ears bare, nothing at the collar); the tips are a little even and gold, leaning late-90s; the top is slightly clumped; and the face itself, as in S4, is broader and reads nearer 30 than the concept's narrow 25.

sections.name: Hair: the curls made in Blender failed three times
sections.note: Your ruling was curls made in Blender. Three attempts, the last after research into how a 1990 shampoo-and-set is made (on rollers: shape by region, a side parting, the ends rolled under), all fail at a glance: above, the third on Sheila's head shows a hard parting, a stiff raised flap, a woven-looking cap, spikes on top and tassels at the back. Under the two-tries rule it is set aside. Sheila does not need it: the face you picked, S4, wears a short, soft, side-swept cut close to her portrait. (A) Epic's own MetaHuman haircuts, free: Sheila keeps S4's, and Darren wears the short cut just above (recommended; done meanwhile). (B) Keep at curls made in Blender, for Darren's grown-out perm: days, and uncertain.

sections.name: The street's name plates: a font's licence
sections.note: The nearest free face to the Kindersley capitals of 1990 street name plates is Marcellus SC, under the SIL Open Font Licence, which lets a game ship a font and is widely used; it is not on LEDGER's licence allowlist, so the plates stay blank until you say. (A) Add the Open Font Licence to the allowlist, for fonts (recommended). (B) No: the plates stay blank.
